correctness.rationale: For every R>0 and -1<=z<1, the axial coordinate is uniform and azimuth independent; tensor contraction yields both exact moment polynomials. Their ratio factorizes into 4(1+t^2)/3, giving bijective inversion. The global 2sqrt3 inequality follows from a nonnegative factored polynomial for all 0<=s<t<1/2, with limiting equality; the angular quarter-power exponent follows from a cosine inequality and its fourth-order full-sphere limit. 2,220 exact-rational comparisons and independent 4D numerical integration checks match the proof, but the universal claim is justified algebraically, not experimentally.

Deriving the result from their forward input is possible; novelty is restricted to the explicit complete inverse theorem, not forward distribution laws.

value.rationale: A complete natural inverse classification of all positive-area spherical-surface caps from the minimum number of even chord moments, with an exact feasibility wedge, explicit reconstruction, sharp global constant for normalized cutoff height and a distinct optimal one-quarter angular exponent at full-sphere degeneration. This resolves both identifiability and conditioning of the two-parameter spherical-cap family; it is not a gratuitous numerical slice or a recomputation of an existing chord table.
